# FNS decay heat

The JAEA Fusion Neutronics Source held a 1 g foil in a 14 MeV field of about
1.1e10 n/cm2/s, withdrew it, and measured the heat its activation products gave
off as it cooled. 73 foils were measured, across three campaigns: two five
minute irradiations followed for about an hour, and one 7.6 hour irradiation
followed out to 400 days.

The benchmark is published by the IAEA through
[CoNDERC](https://nds.iaea.org/conderc/fusion/), and the archive contains
something most benchmark archives do not: **FISPACT-II's own calculated decay
heat**, for every experiment, produced with TENDL-2017. That is what makes the
comparison below a statement about two codes rather than about two libraries.

There is no neutron transport anywhere in this. The benchmark publishes the
spectrum each foil actually saw, so that spectrum is the input.

## yani against FISPACT-II, same library

![yani against FISPACT-II mean deviation](figures/fns-summary.png#only-light)
![yani against FISPACT-II mean deviation](figures/fns-summary-dark.png#only-dark)

On the 130 experiments the archive publishes a FISPACT-II curve for, both codes reading TENDL-2017, yani is closer to the measurement on **64** of them (49%).

| code | experiments | median mean deviation | within 10% | within 20% |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| yani, tendl-2017 | 130 | 10.1% | 63 | 83 |
| FISPACT-II, tendl-2017 | 130 | 10.7% | 63 | 84 |

Both rows are the same experiments with the same evaluations, so the difference is the code.

## Every nuclear-data combination

The row above is the comparison. These are the answer to a different question: given a free choice of data, how close does this get?

| combination | cross sections | reactions | branching | decay | solved | median mean deviation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `tendl-2017` | tendl-2017 | tendl-2017 | tendl-2017 | endf-b8.1 | 132 | 10.1% |

**`tendl-2017`** -- The library FISPACT-II was run with for the published CoNDERC results. This is the apples-to-apples comparison: same cross sections, same reaction topology, same branching, different code.

## Every experiment

One figure per experiment, 132 of them. The solid orange line is the apples-to-apples run and the dashed line is whichever other combination scored best on that foil.

```bash
python benchmarks/fns_decay_heat/sweep.py
```
